events.title: Finland Declares Independence from Russia
events.description: The Finnish Parliament adopted the declaration of independence on December 6, 1917, led by Senate Chairman Pehr Evind Svinhufvud, in the aftermath of the Russian Revolution. Finland was subsequently recognized by Soviet Russia and other nations.
events.significance: Marked the birth of modern Finland as a sovereign state; Finland still celebrates December 6 as its Independence Day.

events.title: Thirteenth Amendment Ratified
events.description: The Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified when Georgia became the 27th state to approve it, reaching the three-fourths threshold needed. It abolished slavery and involuntary servitude except as punishment for a crime.
events.significance: Formally ended chattel slavery in the United States and was the first of the Reconstruction Amendments.

events.title: Edison Demonstrates the Phonograph
events.description: Thomas Edison and his team at Menlo Park, New Jersey, made the first recording of a human voice, reciting 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' on a tinfoil cylinder phonograph. The invention was publicly announced soon after.
events.significance: Launched the era of recorded sound and laid the foundation for the modern recording and music industries.

events.title: Anglo-Irish Treaty Signed
events.description: Representatives of the British government and Irish delegates, including Michael Collins and Arthur Griffith, signed the Anglo-Irish Treaty in London, ending the Irish War of Independence.
events.significance: Established the Irish Free State as a dominion within the British Empire and partitioned Ireland, leading to the Irish Civil War and shaping Irish politics for decades.

events.title: Soviet Counteroffensive at Moscow Begins
events.description: On December 5-6, 1941, Soviet forces under Georgy Zhukov launched a major counteroffensive against German Army Group Centre near Moscow in harsh winter conditions, pushing German troops back from the capital.
events.significance: The first major Soviet strategic success against the Wehrmacht, ending Germany's hope of a quick victory on the Eastern Front.
